## The Problem

I was bored on a road trip and wanted to test whether I could ship something small but genuinely automated end to end: no manual checking, no app to open, just a notification the moment something actually changes. Rain was a clean test case since it's a simple binary state with a real, usable signal.

## What I Built and Why

A PWA where you save a ZIP code, and a GitHub Actions cron job checks that ZIP's weather every 15 minutes via the OpenWeatherMap API. If the rain state flips (starts or stops), it pushes a notification through Firebase Cloud Messaging. Firestore holds the one shared settings doc. No backend server to maintain; the whole thing runs on free-tier scheduled automation.

## How It Went

It works. The full chain (scheduled job, API call, state comparison, push notification) runs on its own with zero upkeep.

## What I'd Do Differently

It's built for one ZIP code and one user by design, since that's all I needed to prove the concept. If I extended it, I'd add per-user settings and auth before letting anyone else use it.

## Tech Stack

React (Vite), Firebase (Firestore + Cloud Messaging), GitHub Actions (cron), OpenWeatherMap API
